localBiteReport: Inshore fishing on Choctawhatchee Bay remains solidly in fall mode as of late November 2026, with water temperature at 69°F. Redfish continue to be the most reliable bay target, with fish holding around bridges, jetties, and East Pass on outgoing tides — a pattern that has stayed consistent since early November according to recent Destin-area charter reports. Speckled trout are an active secondary target, with quality fish in the 22–27 inch range showing up around bait concentrations on the grass flats and in deeper bayous. Sheepshead are building on dock pilings and bridge structure as cooler water moves in, making late November a classic time for that species around the Destin Harbor area. Note that flounder are currently in their fall offshore spawning migration out of the bay, and Florida's inshore flounder harvest season is closed October 15 – November 30, so flounder should be treated as catch-and-release only right now; the most recent regional report (Nov 20–26) confirms fish are actively moving offshore near Santa Rosa Beach and Navarre.
